root_cause.text: smb2_get_ea() in ksmbd failed to validate remaining response buffer space before writing 4-byte EA alignment padding, causing an out-of-bounds write when the EA value consumed the buffer exactly.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (buf_free_len < alignment_bytes) break;` immediately before the previously unconditional `memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes);`, and the CVE/commit text states the existing check was only done before the value `memcpy` while the alignment `memset` could still write 1–3 bytes past `buf_free_len`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a buffer-length check before writing alignment padding in smb2_get_ea to prevent overrunning the output buffer.
intent_record.what: An additional conditional check was inserted before zero-filling alignment padding in smb2_get_ea(): if buf_free_len is less than alignment_bytes, the loop breaks instead of calling memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes) and advancing the buffer pointer and offset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents writing alignment padding when there is not enough remaining buffer space, avoiding a potential out-of-bounds write and stopping further entry packing once the buffer cannot accommodate the required aligned padding.

grouping_result.intent: Add a buffer-length check before writing alignment padding in smb2_get_ea to prevent overrunning the output buffer.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds validation of remaining buffer space before writing the 4-byte EA alignment padding in smb2_get_ea, preventing the out-of-bounds write.

candidates.rationale: This is the actual out-of-bounds write. The function wrote 4-byte alignment padding without first validating that enough response buffer space remained.
This condition allows the padding write path to execute solely based on alignment need, with no accompanying bounds check on remaining buffer space.
This advances the output pointer after the unchecked padding write, reflecting and depending on the same missing bounds validation that can move the pointer past the end of the buffer.
This updates the tracked output size after unchecked padding is added, contributing to incorrect state once the buffer has already been overrun.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct vulnerable write. smb2_get_ea() wrote alignment padding bytes to the response buffer without first checking that sufficient space remained, enabling an out-of-bounds write when the EA data had already consumed the available buffer exactly.
This condition gates the padding-write path based only on alignment need and omits any remaining-buffer validation, allowing the unsafe memset() to execute even when no space is left.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body clearly shows the EA packing logic and the padding write, so it is sufficient to decide. The vulnerable construct is present at lines 4287-4294: after computing `alignment_bytes = ((next_offset + 3) & ~3) - next_offset;`, the code does `memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes);` and only afterwards subtracts `buf_free_len -= alignment_bytes;`. Earlier, the code validates space only for the entry header/name and value: `buf_free_len -= ...name...` (4252-4253), `buf_free_len -= value_len;` (4262), and checks `if (buf_free_len < 0)` only before the value copy (4263-4266). There is no check that `buf_free_len` is at least `alignment_bytes` before the padding write. Therefore, if the EA value exactly consumes the remaining buffer (`buf_free_len == 0` after line 4262), a nonzero `alignment_bytes` will cause `memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes)` at line 4290 to write past the end of the response buffer. The fix would require validating remaining space before writing padding, but that handling is absent here.
